abstract: OMA is a longstanding resource for inferring and exploring orthologous relationships across the tree of life. Here, we describe recent developments that broaden the comparative genomics information and analyses supported by the OMA ecosystem. The latest OMA release contains 2983 extant genomes and 1226 ancestral genome reconstructions spanning all domains of life, with expanded eukaryotic representation and quality-assessed genome selection. We integrated protein structure-aware information across all proteins in OMA, providing structure-derived 3Di representations and structural alignments for hierarchical orthologous groups. For custom datasets, FastOMA enables scalable orthology across thousands of genomes, while OrthoXML-tools facilitates interoperable manipulation and downstream analysis of orthology data. Building on previous resources for ancestral gene repertoire and gene order reconstruction, an extended chromosome viewer enables richer exploration of gene order in extant and reconstructed ancestral genomes, including gene adjacency evolution and integrated downstream analyses. Functional analysis has been extended through the OMA REST API, enabling customizable Gene Ontology enrichment analyses of extant and ancestral gene sets. Finally, updated training resources and support for private deployments broaden access to the OMA ecosystem. Together, these developments provide an integrated framework for studying gene families and genome evolution from sequences, structures, and evolutionary context. OMA is freely accessible at https://omabrowser.org/.
